task.description: Write a genuine fail-then-pass regression test for ISS-0048's actual fix (the owner-crash-reclaim mechanism), not the existing test that was merely reworked to avoid a false positive. The test must: (1) claim a sandbox schema from a helper process, (2) kill that process via an exit signal the pre-fix code could not have caught (e.g. Process.exit(pid, :kill), or letting a spawned process crash/die without calling release/2 -- NOT a raised exception, since try/rescue already handled that path before this fix), (3) assert the claimed schema is reclaimed (dropped from Postgres, or at minimum removed from the pool's active state so a subsequent claim/2 can succeed / the schema no longer physically exists) within a reasonable wait window. Per WF-03 Step 4's requirement, PROVE this is fail-then-pass: check out the pre-fix commit (before ef1e4c8, i.e. the commit at the start of this run's branch -- find it via git log/git merge-base with main) in a temporary way that doesn't disturb the current branch state (e.g. git worktree add, or git stash + checkout + checkout back, or git show <commit>:lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex to a scratch location and run the test against it directly if that's simpler -- your call on the safest mechanical approach), run the new test against pre-fix sandbox_pool.ex and confirm it FAILS, then run it against the current post-fix code on this branch and confirm it PASSES. State both results with real command output in your handoff, not asserted from reading the code.

result.summary:
Added a genuine kill-based regression test to test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs, describe "owning process killed between claim/2 and release/2 (ISS-0048 regression)": claims from a spawn/1-ed process (not Task.async, not the test process), relays the claim back via send/receive rendezvous, then Process.exit(owner_pid, :kill)s it (an exit signal, NOT a raised exception -- try/rescue already handled that path before this fix) and asserts (1) the schema is dropped from real Postgres (polled via a new wait_until_schema_dropped/2 helper, matching the file's existing wait_until_waiter_queued/2 bounded-polling idiom) and (2) the freed quota slot is immediately claimable again with a different sandbox_id, proving the active map entry itself was removed. Also added test/specs/ISS-0048.md with full criterion/rationale/fail-then-pass evidence.

FAIL-THEN-PASS PROOF (real command output):

Pre-fix: checked out merge-base-with-main commit bc7705d (strictly before ef1e4c8, which introduces the owner-monitor fix) into a scratch git worktree at /tmp/sandbox-prefix, copied the current post-fix test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs (including the new test) into it unchanged, symlinked deps/_build from the main checkout, left lib/letflow/sandbox_pool.ex at its pre-fix bc7705d state, and ran the full file against the already-running docker-compose Postgres:

$ cd /tmp/sandbox-prefix && mix test test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs --seed 0
...
  1) test owning process killed between claim/2 and release/2 (ISS-0048 regression) a killed owner's claim is reclaimed: schema dropped and quota slot freed for a subsequent claim/2 (Letflow.SandboxPoolTest)
     test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:367
     expected schema sandbox_8d8e0e2042c1442a86e0bbab4f9b851a to be dropped by SandboxPool's owner-crash reclaim, but it still exists in information_schema.schemata
     code: wait_until_schema_dropped(schema_name)
     stacktrace:
       test/letflow/sandbox_pool_test.exs:407: (test)

(Only the new test failed; the other 7 pre-existing tests passed unchanged pre-fix.) Worktree removed afterward (git worktree remove /tmp/sandbox-prefix --force) -- current branch state was never touched.
